instrument: RIPE Atlas one-off sslcert (SNI), worldwide; reconciled against per-pointer fetch

exception.public_note: On 25 August 2026 this endpoint presented a certificate for its own name to none of the 479 probes in 75 countries: 477 saw a certificate for another name, which is withheld, and 2 saw none. Its operator was notified on 25 August 2026.

methodology: A bare TLS probe with no SNI reports CDN default certificates as defects; even with SNI, cloud routing can hand a default certificate to some vantages. Every figure here reconciles the Atlas run against a fetch of each pointer's actual URL. After reconciliation, on 25 August 2026, exactly one endpoint failed from every vantage and every method; all others validated when fetched the way software fetches them, with SNI.

correction.what: The counts were a snapshot taken while the one-off measurements were still collecting results (459 of 478; 476; 74 countries). They now hold the final counts from the RIPE Atlas API: 460 of 479 for the control, 0 of 479 for the exception (477 another name, 2 none), 75 countries. The exception is no longer gated and its note no longer says the operator will be notified: it was notified on 25 August 2026. The methodology is dated and in the past tense.
correction.continents_are: probe counts from the snapshot (478 probes), not country counts and not recomputed for the final 479; the later run (16-30) gives country counts.
correction.valid_means: probes whose leaf certificate named the host. Atlas sslcert records the certificate a server presents; it does not validate the chain. The key is kept because existing readers use it; own_name holds the same count.
correction.measured_utc_is: the file's label, which orders the runs; the Atlas result timestamps are in atlas_result_window_utc.
